facts_of_case: The parties were married for three days before separating. They filed a petition under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act for a decree of divorce by mutual consent.

legal_principles.principle: The statutory period of six months specified in Section 13B(2) is directory in nature, but the power to waive it is subject to certain conditions.
legal_principles.held: Thus, it has been held that six months statutory period prescribed is directory in nature.

legal_principles.principle: The court should not grant permission for waiving off the stipulated period of six months under Section 13B(2) if the statutory period of one year under Section 13B is already over before the first motion itself.
legal_principles.held: In such circumstances, this Court cannot grant permission for waiving off the stipulated period of six months under Section 13B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: The court should not grant permission for waiving off the stipulated period of six months under Section 13B(2) if all efforts for mediation/conciliation have failed and there is no likelihood of success in that direction by any further efforts.
legal_principles.held: Thus, it has been held that six months statutory period prescribed is directory in nature.

legal_principles.principle: The court should not grant permission for waiving off the stipulated period of six months under Section 13B(2) if the parties have genuinely settled their differences including alimony, custody of child or any other pending issues between the parties.
legal_principles.held: Thus, it has been held that six months statutory period prescribed is directory in nature.

outcome.final_order: The High Court's order dismissing the Civil Revisional Application was upheld, and the requirement to wait six months before filing the petition was not waived.
